thread:
deploy-bot: [deploy] starting canary rollout r-inference/prod:v2 -> prod-cluster-a (canary 5%) at 2026-03-15T14:02:36Z

alice (sre): Heads up — canary pods entering CrashLoopBackOff almost immediately. seeing SIGKILL in kubelet logs.

carol (monitoring): Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/canary-overview?orgId=1 shows spike in restarts and 502s from ingress for canary host. Error rate up ~12% on the canary slice.

bob (eng-runtime): ugh, I changed the liveness probe path in the manifest to /healthz which now calls the model warmup. that warmup can take ~8-12s on cold-start; liveness was 5s. looks like pods are getting killed before warmup finishes. My bad.

incident-bot: paging oncall -> @oncall_sre : High error rate for r-inference canary, CrashLoopBackOff observed (auto-created incident INC-2026-045).

oncall_sre: I'm on it. can you post `kubectl describe pod <pod>` logs for one of the failing pods? Also what's the canary percentage?

alice (sre): canary is 5%. grabbing pod info now.

alice (sre): ```
Name: r-inference-canary-5b7f6
State: Waiting
  Reason: CrashLoopBackOff
Last Termination State: Terminated
  Reason: Killed
  Signal: 9
  Exit Code: 137
Events:
  Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
  Back-off restarting failed container
```

bob (eng-runtime): Exit code 137 == SIGKILL, likely from kubelet killing container after liveness failure. confirm that /healthz returns 500 during warmup.

carol (monitoring): Also seeing concurrent HPA scale-down activity earlier which reduced pods to 1 then new replica tried to start under pressure. Not sure if HPA interplay made it worse.

dave (eng-platform): Two immediate mitigation options: 1) flip the feature flag to disable the v2 healthcheck endpoint (LD flag -> r_inference.use_new_healthz=false) which makes container respond quickly, or 2) abort/rollback the rollout to v1 which has the old probe. Which do we want?

bob (eng-runtime): Given the unknowns, I prefer rollback first to restore stability. we can later re-release with a safe probe timeout.

product-ops: customer impact? any user-facing errors we should surface?

cs_lead: We're seeing increased 502s for a handful of enterprise customers in NA region (alerts from sentry + customer reports). Recommend status page update: "Degraded — inference requests intermittently failing for a subset of customers."

oncall_sre: initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rolling back rollout r-inference/prod:v2 -> previous revision (undo) at 2026-03-15T14:08:12Z

alice (sre): kubectl output: `deployment.apps/r-inference: rolling back to revision 42`

deploy-bot: rollback progressing — new replicaset stabilizing.

carol (monitoring): metrics starting to recover: error rate back down to baseline for non-canary traffic. canary host still garbage until pods replaced.

dave (eng-platform): For postmortem, propose a guard in the rollout pipeline to validate liveness timeout >= observed cold-start + buffer. also add a preflight e2e that exercises /healthz warmup path.

bob (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll open a PR to revert the changed probe and set default initialDelaySeconds=15 and timeoutSeconds=3. also will add a feature-flag gated rollout in future.

incident-bot: INC-2026-045 updated: severity -> P2 (customer impacting intermittently), assigned to eng-runtime and infra.

product-ops: Posting status page update now: "We are rolling back a recent inference rollout that caused elevated error rates for some customers. No broad data loss. Eng teams are mitigating; updates to follow."

cs_lead: I'll notify affected customers with the known window and workaround (retry/backoff).

alice (sre): Confirming pods stabilized on previous revision at 14:12:00Z. No additional crashloops.

oncall_sre: Great work folks. next actions: 1) bob to PR probe change + tests, 2) dave to add pipeline preflight, 3) eng-sre to run a canary with extended probe in staging and promote. assign postmortem owner?

bob (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem. will include timeline, root cause (probe change and HPA interplay), and mitigation (rollback, probe defaults, pipeline checks).

product-ops: closing this channel for now. leave incident open for postmortem artifacts. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
